[00:24] Samir Patel: The three big priorities for Q4 are: one, continue pushing Private deployments - customers in regulated verticals expect higher control; two, Dedicated capacity improvements for predictable latency; and three, Redwood Optimize, which is our cost/perf toolkit to help customers tune batching and quantization.

[01:36] Maya Alvarez: Ops update - Dedicated autoscaling policies are in pilot with two customers, burst capacity and predictable throughput are working but we need better cost attribution. also rolling out more VPC templates for private control plane installs. there was a question earlier about on-prem packaging and air-gapped installs - yes, we have a path but it's longer lead time.

[02:05] Evan Kim: Sales notes - pipeline is healthy, major push on mid-market companies using dedicated pools. renewals are stable, we had a couple of expansion wins tied to latency SLOs. pricing conversations keep coming back to cost vs latency tradeoffs; customers ask about when to pick dedicated vs hosted - typical guidance: hosted for fast time-to-value, dedicated for predictable p99 and data isolation.

[02:35] Rina Gupta: CS shoutouts - we've onboarded three new enterprise CSMs this month, and launched a retention playbook focused on early workload profiling which reduces surprises during production rollouts.

[02:50] Samir Patel: Quick org note - a few leadership adjustments: Jordan will lead product and roadmap coordination, Maya elevated to lead infra ops, and we'll consolidate platform engineering under Priya for tighter runtime-to-deploy integrations. we'll post an org chart in the people-docs channel.
